messages:
maya: quick thread — thinking about refactoring the onboarding pipeline dependency graph to be DAG-first instead of the current linear stages. motivation: we waste compute re-running benches when only a downstream adapter changed.

ravi: +1. can you outline concrete tradeoffs? latency to accept vs complexity?

maya: short list: 1) benefits: cacheable artifacts per node, partial re-run, parallelizable. 2) downsides: scheduler complexity, harder to reason about failure modes, more metadata to track (fingerprints, inputs).

chris: how do you plan to handle bench/regression signals? bench currently assumes full-run golden set.

maya: propose node-level versioning + a "provenance manifest". each bench node declares input fingerprints; if fingerprints unchanged we skip. golden/regression run becomes final "quality gate" node that depends on core outputs.

maya: draft manifest example:
```
{"node": "quantize", "inputs": ["model-v1"], "fingerprint": "sha256:abcd1234"}
```

lin: what about compatibility checks — model ABI mismatches? do we need a separate compatibility node early in the DAG?

maya: yes — compatibility lint node should be first-level. it emits a compatibility token that downstream nodes consume. It prevents wasted work if model fails quick checks.

kevin: curious about storage/cost — caching artifacts per node increases storage. estimate?

maya: initial rough calc: avg artifact 200MB, ~1000 new models/mo -> 200GB/mo. we can TTL and zstd; also keep only latest per variant. cost seems manageable vs repeated bench cost.

admit-bot: FYI: existing intake jobs currently take ~45m total on average, with bench worker reuse at 12 tokens/s.

ravi: how does this affect canaries and rollouts? can we stage nodes to support canary-only artifacts?

maya: yes — DAG allows conditional branches. canary branch can point to lighter bench nodes and full-eval later. rollout controller reads final gate result.

chris: what about observability? need per-node traces, flakiness metrics, and quick rerun endpoints.

maya: agree — propose: per-node traces in telemetry, expose single-click rerun that accepts node list, and UI shows provenance graph.

lin: sounds good. next steps?

maya: i'll put together an RFC draft with schema for node manifests, fingerprinting rules, and a PoC scheduler. volunteers to review: @ravi @chris @lin @kevin. aiming to ship PoC in 4 weeks. :calendar:

ravi: I'll review.

chris: count me in.

lin: can help with compatibility linting.

kevin: happy to look at storage TTLs.
